data.name: Aslan
data.gender_notes: Aslan is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Turkish and other Turkic languages, Aslan means 'lion'. In Islamic culture, the lion is a symbol of courage, power, and pride. The lion is mentioned in the Quran, and the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is described as a 'seal of prophets' and a 'lion among men'. The name Aslan carries the meaning “Lion” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Aslan usually hope their child will grow to embody lion and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of courage and strength in the faith.
data.etymology: Aslan belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lion.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aslan total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_urdu.name: اسلم

data.cultural_impact: The name Aslan is culturally significant as it is derived from the Turkish and other Turkic languages where it means 'lion'. In Islamic culture, the lion is a powerful and courageous symbol that represents strength, dignity, and and fearlessness. Aslan is also the name of a popular character in Turkish folklore and literature, who is known for his bravery and unwavering loyalty.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic terminology, the name Aslan holds deep spiritual significance as it is reminiscent of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), who is described in hadith as a 'seal of the prophets' and 'a lion among men' for his unwavering courage, determination, and leadership in spreading the message of Islam. The lion is also mentioned in the Quran, where it is praised for its noble characteristics and strength, and is used as a metaphor for those who strive to defend their faith and communities with courage and conviction. Aslan thus represents the qualities of the courageous Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and those who embody his ideals.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Battuta's Travels: Ibn Battuta describes Aslan as a local ruler in the city of Balans, located in present-day Burkina Faso. The time period for this reference is around 1353 AD.
historical_references.context: Ibn Battuta, a famous Moroccan traveler, visited various parts of the Islamic world including West Africa. During his travels, he encountered a local ruler in the city of Balans, whom he referred to as Aslan.

historical_references.reference: Al-Biruni's India: Al-Biruni mentions Aslan as the founder of Alamut, a city in present-day Iran. The time period for this reference is around 1032 AD.
historical_references.context: Al-Biruni, a Persian scholar, wrote a comprehensive account of India. In his work, he mentions Aslan as the founder of Alamut, a city located in present-day Iran. Aslan is believed to have established the Nizari Ismaili state in Alamut.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Aslan' is derived from the Islamic tradition and translates to 'lion.' In modern popular culture, Aslan is most notably recognized as the main character in 'The Chronicles of Narnia' book series by C.S. Lewis. The character is depicted as a talking lion who is also the Christian deity Aslan and is seen as a symbol of courage and leadership. Aslan is also a major character in the animated series 'The Lion Guard,' which is a spin-off from Disney's 'The Lion King.' In video games, Aslan is featured in 'Lion's Pride'' and 'Lion's Roar II,' which are role-playing games that allow players to control and develop their own Aslan characters, further emphasizing the symbolism and influence of the name in modern society.
